oneliner.t: Birmingham Republican and career educator (teacher, school administrator, assistant superintendent, college professor) making her first run for public office.

upbringing.t: Early-life details are not documented in the sources reached. Her candidate profile lists her as 44, with a 2003 special-education degree from the University of Alabama and a 2012 doctorate in education from Samford. She is developing 'Hub in the Hills,' a shared nonprofit campus she founded with her husband, and chairs the board of Unless U, a program for adults with disabilities.

career.role: Teacher, elementary administrator, assistant superintendent, college professor

career.org: Hub in the Hills (nonprofit shared campus)

platform.t: Address rising housing, grocery, utility, transportation and child-care costs through responsible federal spending and less unnecessary regulation.
Support small businesses and strong local economies.
Strengthen cooperation among teachers, parents, school leaders and communities; named improving education a top priority.
Give law enforcement, firefighters and EMS the resources they need.
Strengthen rural hospitals and improve access for people who travel farthest for care.
Campaign focus includes support for agriculture and industry and responsive leadership.

promises.t: Make sure the district is "never taken for granted" and campaign to earn every voter's trust.

claims.claim: "Congresswoman Sewell has been in office for over 15 years."

said.where: Primary-night statement, reported by BirminghamWatch and 1819 News

record.t: Sewell took office January 3, 2011, so she has served about 15 years and 9 months as of October 2026.

claims.claim: Industry, agriculture and communities in the district have struggled during Sewell's tenure.

said.where: Primary-night statement, reported by BirminghamWatch and 1819 News

record.t: Too general to test against a specific dataset as stated.

record.t: Single candidate-supplied source. No registrar or dissertation record was reached.

The district has lacked "proactive representation" in Washington.

record.t: A characterization, not a checkable fact.

aipac_endorse.t: Not listed — she does not appear on Track AIPAC (as of 2026-10-08); AIPAC's endorsement page was not checked.

aipac_pac.note: 2026 cycle: FEC shows $0 from any PAC or committee through Jul 22, 2026

udp.note: Not listed on Track AIPAC; no UDP spending found in sources reached.

fec.history_note: First federal race; principal committee Akin for Congress (C00953315), coverage Apr 1–Jul 22, 2026. The $100,000 is a candidate loan, still owed to her. $500 in individual refunds. In the primary, opponent David Perry said she had raised $138,000 (BirminghamWatch). That figure differs from FEC's $150,730 total and its $50,730 in contributions, and is not used. Outside spending: none found.
fec.self_note: Candidate money here is a loan to the campaign, which can be repaid from later donations.

note.t: No House candidate financial disclosure was located; the Clerk's search form could not be used. No net-worth or asset data.
Lives in Birmingham, part of which is in AL-07. University of Alabama (Tuscaloosa) and Samford (Birmingham) degrees. Years of residence not documented.

checks.legal: Not done. CourtListener is blocked, Justia was not reached, Alacourt is paywalled, and no news search for lawsuits or charges was possible (search budget exhausted). Nothing turned up in the Reflector, BirminghamWatch, 1819 News or ADN coverage reviewed.
checks.foreign: No financial disclosure located; FARA blocked. Nothing found in news reviewed.
checks.claims: The mechanical sample could not be run: akinforcongress.com could not be fetched (not in the tool's allowed set), and no ads were found. Fallback: her candidate-supplied BirminghamWatch profile plus statements quoted in Aug 11–12, 2026 coverage. Seven claims; five are checkable. Oct 8 pass: akinforcongress.com was still blocked; BirminghamWatch's profile confirms that URL as her site. The profile's five issue statements were reviewed in order: lower housing, grocery, utility, transportation and child-care costs through responsible spending and less regulation; support small business; education partnerships; resources for police, fire and EMS; strengthen rural hospitals. All are positions, not checkable facts. Also re-read the 1819 News, Reflector, ADN and BirminghamWatch primary-night stories, which contain no further factual claims. No new claims added. Total: 7 claims, 1 rated true, 4 unverifiable, 2 opinion.
checks.democracy: Reviewed her BirminghamWatch profile and the 1819 News, Reflector, ADN and BirminghamWatch stories from August 2026. None contains a statement on the 2020 or 2024 results. Her campaign site was unreachable, and new news searches could not be run.

recordx.note: No sitting-member record. FEC RFAI/notices not checked. House candidate financial-disclosure timeliness not determined.

research_notes: Ethics is 'na': she has never held office, so House Ethics and the Alabama Ethics Commission don't apply. The BirminghamWatch profile is candidate-supplied, so the bio items carry 'unverifiable' verdicts until employment and degree records are checked. Same depth and source set as the other AL-06/AL-07 candidates. WEB LIMITS (Oct 8, 2026 pass): the shared web-search budget was used up, and outbound connections to campaign sites, web.archive.org, census.gov, bls.gov, congress.gov and the House Clerk's disclosure search were blocked or refused. CLAIMS: only 1 rated verdict. Her published material available here is mostly positions and characterizations of Sewell, but the campaign site was never reached, so this is not a confirmed 'publishes fewer than 5' finding; checklist.claims stays 'news'. The bio claims (UA 2003, Samford Ed.D. 2012, career posts, nonprofit roles) need registrar, dissertation and IRS Form 990 checks. DISCLOSURES: candidate financial disclosure not located; stays 'no'. DEMOCRACY: set to 'news'; no results statement found in coverage reviewed.
